A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same Fed-NGA work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison. The substantial theoretical and experimental revisions do not prevent matching retained content.

before.justification: V1 reports original MNIST experiments with LeNet and MLP, including accuracy under Byzantine attacks, heterogeneity sensitivity, and aggregation timing in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 reports original accuracy and aggregation-time experiments on MNIST, CIFAR10, and TinyImageNet under multiple attacks and heterogeneity settings, including extensive results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The operative Fed-NGA mechanism remains client-gradient upload, individual normalization, weighted aggregation, and model broadcast. V2 explicitly writes sampled subdatasets and stochastic gradients into Algorithm 1, but v1 already documents minibatch training in Appendix B. This clarifies the stochastic formulation without establishing a new aggregation component or newly introduced empirical sampling procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds CIFAR10 and TinyImageNet image classification to the original MNIST coverage. MNIST experiments with both LeNet and MLP remain in Appendix C. Evaluation also adds LIE and FoE adversarial scenarios alongside the retained Gaussian, Same-value, and Sign-flip attacks.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates FedAvg, Median, Krum, and Geometric Median against Fed-NGA. V2 retains these and adds Maximum Correntropy Aggregation (MCA) and Centered Clipping (CClip), including in the retained MNIST comparisons in Table 4. These are evaluated comparators, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: Appendix B changes the client count from 100 to 50, batch size from 512 to 32, and MNIST training budget from 10,000 to 500 iterations. The common constant learning rate of 0.02 becomes separate decaying schedules for Fed-NGA and baselines. MNIST MLP dimensions and the Gaussian attack distribution also change; new datasets receive explicit model configurations and budgets.

E4.justification: The existing attack-intensity and heterogeneity sweeps are substantially extended to LIE/FoE robustness and interactions across three datasets. Appendix C also expands a single aggregation-timing comparison into systematic analysis across attack types, intensities, and heterogeneity. The new stress tests expose severe TinyImageNet failures under high attack ratios, extending the questions addressed by v1's MNIST analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or specified significance tests. V2 introduces statements about statistically significant gains, but supplies no corresponding statistical procedure or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the MNIST results under revised protocols and adds extensive accuracy and timing results. For MNIST/LeNet at beta = 0.6 without attacks, Fed-NGA changes from 98.38% in v1 to 98.50% in v2 Table 4, with FedAvg changing from leading to trailing; this is not a same-setting improvement. New TinyImageNet results include 0.50% for Fed-NGA versus 31.63% for Krum under Sign-flip at attack ratio 0.4 and beta = 0.6.

T1.justification: V2 removes the strongly convex theorem, bounded-gradient assumption, and associated lemma/proofs. It introduces unbiased stochastic gradients and Type I/II noise and heterogeneity assumptions. New Theorem 3.7 gives a residual bound depending on noise and heterogeneity; Theorem 3.9 extends v1's directional non-convex result with stochastic directional error. Appendices E and F are substantially revised, and the old Appendix G is removed.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes zero-gap convergence for non-convex objectives and linear zero-gap convergence under strong convexity. V2 drops the strongly convex claim and distinguishes general convergence to a neighborhood from exact stationarity under additional directional conditions. The central normalized-aggregation mechanism, linear aggregation complexity, and Byzantine/non-IID robustness claims remain.

C2.justification: V1 presents directional heterogeneity as a relaxed assumption. V2 Appendix A and Remark 3.10 discuss how its restrictiveness depends on gradient norms and why exact convergence requires suitable bounds throughout training. V2 also adds architecture-based interpretations of TinyImageNet failures and explicitly identifies broader zero-gap guarantees as a limitation. Some robustness interpretations remain overstated relative to the tables.

D1.justification: Appendix B substantially expands reproducibility information, including dataset-specific architectures and learning-rate schedules, GM/MCA tolerance of 10^-5, LIE and FoE coefficients, and TensorFlow versus NumPy implementations for timing. Hardware and PyTorch version remain unchanged. These disclosures accompany the experimental revisions without establishing changes to previously unspecified implementations.

R1.justification: V2 adds substantive positioning against normalization research in optimization and federated learning, including work by Cutkosky and Mehta, Dai, Jakovetic, Li, and Wang. Table 1 and Appendix D add MCA/CClip and revise median-based aggregation complexity from O(pM) to O(pM log M), strengthening the claimed computational distinction from prior methods.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, results discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. The theory is reorganized around two assumption families, Appendix C is reorganized by attack performance, timing, and heterogeneity, and Appendix A is repurposed. The old notation definition moves into the main text, and the contents page is removed.

P2.justification: V2 restructures Table 1, reorganizes accuracy tables around methods and attack ratios, and adds extensive timing tables. The repeated learning-curve grids are replaced by a different mixture of attack-ratio plots, convergence plots, and grouped timing charts. A new geometric illustration appears as Figure 5. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical replacement or renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves applicability assessment through broader adversarial evaluation that reveals failure regimes beyond v1's MNIST experiments. It also removes the problematic linear-to-zero claim—v1 Remark 3.8 gives a nonzero constant-step residual—and separates general neighborhood convergence from conditional exact stationarity. Expanded implementation details improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh remaining weaknesses, including absent uncertainty reporting, overbroad robustness prose, and new reporting inconsistencies: Table 6 gives 2.20% for TinyImageNet Same-value at beta = 0.6 and attack ratio 0.4, while Figure 11(b) plots roughly 24%.
